title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident shows a deliberate attempt to manipulate the training data or retrieval inputs of AI chatbots by flooding the information environment with fabricated institutional content. A nonexistent think tank published an extraordinarily large volume of text in a very short time, framed as neutral scholarship, with the explicit goal of causing AI systems to cite that content as authoritative. The failure this exposes is not in any single AI model's reasoning but in the broader ecosystem: AI systems that surface or cite sources can be gamed when the source appears credible on the surface and volume substitutes for legitimacy.

The operation worked at the input layer of AI deployment, before any model evaluation of source integrity. Catching it would have required AI systems or their operators to verify that cited institutions actually exist, or to weight sources by independent corroboration rather than textual volume and surface plausibility. Neither of those checks appears to have been in place.

What is not established is whether any specific AI company was aware of the campaign, whether the content was incorporated into training data or only retrieved at inference time, and whether the operation violated any law, as the reporting describes the campaign without documenting a legal finding or platform ruling against it.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

An Israeli-funded fake think tank called the Hanover Institute published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days, designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots into making pro-Israel arguments. The nonexistent institute presented one-sided research on controversial topics including Palestinian torture, Israeli war crimes, and Gaza starvation, framing Israel's position as neutral scholarship. The operation used a platform optimized to get AI systems to cite the content, and was funded through European advertising company Havas Media, with American firms including Piro Inc managing the campaign.

Israeli officials later expressed doubts about the strategy's effectiveness, with government spending on the broader public diplomacy effort reaching hundreds of millions of dollars. American public opinion has shifted significantly against Israel, with polls showing Palestinians gaining more support and unfavorable views of Israel rising substantially since 2022. A researcher analyzing the campaign noted that while the effort successfully influences chatbot responses, it has failed to change public opinion polls, suggesting the underlying policies rather than messaging are driving American opposition to Israeli positions.
